analysis: Only CI test files changed: .github/scripts/test-threat-bedrock.py (new MembershipTests and MemberGateTests, new imports of threat_review.membership.active_member and ORGANIZATION_ID, head lines ~265-382) and .github/scripts/test-threat-budget.py (a failure() diagnostics test near line 571). Nothing in the supplied files touches coordinator, provider, attestation, encryption, billing or payment code. The GitHub Actions and review tooling supply chain is out of scope in the canonical scope section, and no canonical TB or T entry covers the PR threat-review gate. The tests describe the intended gate behavior. A clean scan clears a PR only for an active org member, checked live against an org-membership endpoint with a separate membership-only token. Outsider PRs, bots, malformed identities, wrong org, user or role, pending state, and 403/500 responses all fail closed or raise ReviewUnavailable. Outsiders keep the independent human override path. author_association and repo permissions cannot substitute for membership, and the lookup is re-run on every evaluation. The failure() test asserts that provider payload text is not echoed in diagnostics. Coverage limit: the implementation files (threat_review/membership.py, threat-review-gate.py, threat_review/budget_scan.py) were not supplied. A later pass should verify them against these tests, in particular that GH_TOKEN and the membership token stay separated and that a 404 maps to non-member. No product security regression or threat-model gap is evident from the test changes alone.
